accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: hostile relations between the victim's family and the accused, arising from a neighbourhood dispute
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen in company of accused; recovery of blood-stained clothing on information given; motive)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302, 364 and 120-B; life imprisonment under s.302 with fine of Rs.5000 each; RI 7 years under s.364 and 7 years RI under s.120-B (with fines)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302), kidnapping (IPC s.364) and criminal conspiracy (IPC s.120-B), as charged and affirmed for the appellants
neutral_facts: The victim, a seven-year-old boy, left home for school one morning in mid-April and did not return. His father searched relatives and the school without success and reported the boy missing to the police the same day. About five days later, the body of a boy was found on a hillock. The body had been partly eaten by animals, the right hand and head were missing, and the father identified the body from the clothes, shoes, socks and school bag. Three witnesses, two goldsmiths and a firewood collector, said they saw the victim in the company of three men, including the accused, on a scooter or walking towards the hillock around midday. The witnesses knew the accused and the victim, and one witness was cross-examined at length without any contradiction of his account. Following information given by one of the accused, a blood-stained pant and shirt were recovered from that accused's house in the presence of two witnesses. A forensic report found the blood on them to be of human origin. The victim's family had a prior dispute with the accused over a neighbourhood incident in which a girl died after consuming poison. One accused had threatened to finish the victim's family. The victim's mother said she saw the accused with a scooter near her house on the day the victim went missing.
physical_harm: Death of the seven-year-old victim; body mutilated, right hand and head missing, partly eaten by animals
motive: Enmity from a neighbourhood dispute over a girl's death by poison and threats to finish the victim's family (accepted by the court as proved)
key_evidence_accepted: Last-seen evidence of PW-3, PW-4 and PW-10; recovery of blood-stained pant and shirt with FSL report of human blood; motive evidence of PW-1 and PW-7
witness_credibility: PW-10 cross-examined at length with nothing disproving his statement; PW-3 and PW-4 did not identify the accused in the identification parade but their assertions were accepted; inconsistencies about the body's condition attributed to villager witnesses and were not held fatal
post_offence_conduct: Not stated for the appellants; blood-stained clothing recovered from a house on information given by A-1, who did not appeal
trial_duration: offence: 15.04.1998; trial judgment: 31.01.2002; High Court: 02.03.2006; Supreme Court: not given
legal_representation: Seeraj Bagga (amicus curiae) for the appellants; Shovan Mishra for the State
investigation_status: Report lodged 16.04.1998; second report 19.04.1998; accused arrested 22.04.1998; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (31.01.2002): convicted and sentenced. High Court (02.03.2006): appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeals of A-2 and A-3 dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Relied on three circumstances: last seen in company of accused, recovery of incriminating articles on information given, and motive. No separate oral argument recorded in the judgment
defence_argument: Amicus contended that absent direct evidence, any discrepancy suggesting two possible views should give the accused benefit of doubt; counsel also pointed to inconsistencies in witnesses' description of the body
legal_principle_applied: Five golden principles for proof by circumstantial evidence: circumstances fully established and consistent only with guilt, conclusive, excluding every other hypothesis, forming a complete chain
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra, (1984) 4 SCC 116; Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade v. State of Maharashtra, (1973) 2 SCC 793 (as cited within Sharda)
sentencing_rationale: Not stated; court held the life sentence was rightly awarded and affirmed without separate sentencing reasoning
